summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — DELL +33%, NTAP +22%, NOW +14%, IBM +13%, HPE +13%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (CLX -6%, RMD -6%, INTC -5%, TPR -5%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: DELL (+32.76%) — Q1 FY27 earnings beat: revenue $43.8B (+88% YoY), AI server revenue $16.1B (+757%), $24.4B new AI orders booked, FY27 guidance raised to $167B midpoint; Susquehanna upgraded to Positive, PT $138→$700. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — DELL is a mega-cap AI infrastructure hardware name with no current coverage. The +32% move gapped in on the first trading day after earnings released May 28–29 after hours, requiring pre-market or open-print positioning to achieve a meaningful fill.

top_movers.suggestion: Introduce an earnings-watchlist overlay for mega-cap AI hardware names (DELL, HPE, SMCI, etc.): on a post-results gap ≥20% at open, take a scaled long if first-15-min volume ≥2× 20-day average, with a hard 5% stop and same-day exit rule.

top_movers.catalyst: NetApp Q4 FY2026 beat (EPS $2.43 vs $2.27 est., rev $1.95B vs $1.87B); record FY26 revenue $6.93B, bullish FY27 guidance, and analyst PT raises to $199–$200 (Argus, Barclays) drove continued post-earnings re-rating.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe (~$38B large-cap infrastructure/storage). The primary gap occurred at the May 30 open (earnings reported May 29 after close); by June 1 the initial gap-reaction window had closed and RSI was severely extended after a multi-session surge.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-earnings drift sleeve: re-enter names with Day-1 earnings gap ≥15% if Day-2/3 volume confirms at ≥1.2× 20-day average, capping position at 0.5× normal size; this catches multi-day re-rating without requiring pre-earnings positioning.

top_movers.catalyst: ServiceNow's Knowledge 2026 conference unveiled new gen-AI tools (Otto assistant) and partnerships; a $4.2B buyback was approved; BofA reinstated with Buy; and Snowflake's blowout Q1 sparked a broad enterprise-AI sector rally.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. NOW is a large-cap enterprise SaaS name excluded by the bot's probable small/mid-cap universe cap. The move was also multi-driver (conference catalyst + buyback + sector contagion from Snowflake), requiring pre-event positioning rather than reactive signal.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a large-cap news-reactive tier gated on ≥+5% pre-market gap with ≥1.5× avg volume; seed it with enterprise-software names around their annual user-conference dates (Knowledge, Dreamforce) so multi-driver gap-ups like this are eligible for a same-day momentum entry.

top_movers.catalyst: Barclays initiated IBM at Overweight ($350 PT) and a resurfaced Trump video praising CEO Arvind Krishna went viral simultaneously, triggering a premarket spike of up to 15% on top of IBM's +30% May rally.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — IBM is a Dow-30 mega-cap (~$270B) beyond typical cap filters. The dual catalyst (analyst initiation + viral social-media clip) was a pure intraday event with no prior-session momentum signal to pre-position from.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an analyst-initiation scanner: flag Dow-30/S&P-100 names with fresh Overweight initiations at open; enter on confirmed ≥1.5× ADV volume in the first 30 min with gap ≥5%, capping size at 0.5× normal given social-media noise risk.

top_movers.catalyst: Dell's May-29 AI-server blowout (AI revenue +757% YoY, orders $24B) sparked sector sympathy; HPE's own $5B AI backlog and Juniper networking synergies fueled a pre-earnings short squeeze ahead of its after-close Q2 report.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — HPE is a large-cap S&P 500 enterprise-tech name likely beyond the bot's sector or cap filters. The move was also a pre-earnings gap triggered by a peer's overnight result, requiring pre-open positioning before any intraday signal could form.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a sector-sympathy gate: when an AI-infrastructure peer (Dell, Cisco, Arista) beats quarterly revenue by >10%, flag sector-adjacent large-caps with AI-server exposure for next-session momentum entry in the first 30 minutes of open.

top_movers.catalyst: Q1 FY2027 beat-and-raise: EPS $2.66 vs $2.52 est, revenue +13.5% YoY, AI product ACV +200% YoY, non-GAAP operating margin guidance raised to ~30.5%, plus $1B buyback reaffirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — WDAY is a $30B+ large-cap enterprise-software name unlikely to appear on momentum or mean-reversion screens. The +12% move was a post-earnings gap-up priced in at Friday's close; no intraday signal could have anticipated it without pre-earnings positioning.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an earnings-gap capture rule: for large-cap software names (mkt cap >$10B) reporting a beat-and-raise with EPS surprise ≥3%, enter long on Monday open if close-to-close gap is +8–20% and volume is ≥2× 20-day avg, with a tight 4% stop to limit chasing risk.

top_movers.catalyst: CEO Linda Rendle announced May 28 she is stepping down for health reasons, triggering a ~6.4% sell-off on June 1; move compounded by a pre-existing lowered FY2026 outlook (−6% net sales, −24–27% EPS) and analyst price-target cuts from Goldman, Morgan Stanley, and JPMorgan.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — CLX is a large-cap (~$11B) consumer staples name not covered by momentum or mean-reversion screens. top_movers.suggestion: Add a pre-market 8-K event scanner that flags S&P 500 names with CEO-departure or material-guidance-cut filings overnight and places a momentum-short entry at open if the implied gap exceeds −4%, capped at 0.5× normal position size for defensive-sector names.

top_movers.catalyst: Noctrix Health ($340M) acquisition closed ~June 1, adding M&A dilution overhang on top of post-Q3 revenue-miss selling (Q3 rev ~$1.43B, below est.) and CFO retirement; stock breached 52-week low, triggering technical stop-outs.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — RMD is a large-cap (~$28B) medical-device name not covered by current sector filters. top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-earnings-drift screen: flag large-cap healthcare names with revenue miss + net-insider-selling + price within 5% of 52-week low within 30 days of earnings, and route them into the short-side watchlist if short capability exists — else mark as 'avoid-long' to prevent counter-trend longs.

top_movers.catalyst: Nvidia unveiled RTX Spark at Computex — an Arm/Blackwell SoC for Windows laptops co-developed with Microsoft — directly threatening Intel's PC CPU core business and sending INTC down ~6% at open.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. The -5.14% drop was a sudden competitive-threat catalyst (Nvidia Computex reveal) requiring a pre-market short entry; the bot's likely long-only constraints make this structurally untradeable.
top_movers.suggestion: No actionable change — catching this requires short capability; if shorts are enabled, add a semiconductor news gate that triggers on major competitor product reveals (Computex/CES) and opens a short within 30 min of market open.

top_movers.catalyst: Post-Q3 profit-taking momentum continues: stock had already fallen ~10% on May 7 earnings day (sell-the-news despite a large beat), and CEO Todd Kahn's $2.74M insider sale disclosed May 30 amplified bearish sentiment into June.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — Tapestry (~$29B market cap, consumer discretionary luxury) is not covered. The move is a post-earnings drift pattern (second leg of the May 7 sell-the-news drop), a dynamic requiring earnings-event decay tracking rather than intraday signal generation.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-earnings drift watchlist: flag large-cap consumer discretionary names that gap down >8% on earnings day and are still in negative momentum after 15+ sessions; route to a short-side or underweight signal if insider selling corroborates within the window.
